pr_title: udev: manipulate device nodes with O_PATH
pr_body:
This is one of bunch of fixes that hopefully will eventually fix #16858. It's just one small part of a whole though, and a proper fix requires more work.

The main goal with this is to minimize a race where the kernel creates a device node in devtmpfs for us, and we then adjust its ownership/access mode/ACLs/timestamps but in the middle of it the kernel replaces the device node with a new one, and we apply half of it.

This doesn't fix the race fully (we can't, after all the kernel doesn't hand us a ready O_PATH fd to the device node), but it does two things:

1. we'll adjust the node in full now or not at all. we'll not apply partial settings to device nodes (which is problematic security-wise)

2. this removes an error condition where the handler would return EEXIST if the node is replaced in the middle, thus failing the rule application. We now operate systematically: either we apply the rules or we don't because the node went away, but we'll never fail because of it. 

Or to summarize: it's atomic and graceful now, in all conditions: either it's applied or not applied, and if something vanishes in the middle this neither causes an error nor results in partially applied props.
